title: Gleason: extremally disconnected equals projective
statement:
Let $S$ be a compact Hausdorff space. The following are equivalent.

1. $S$ is extremally disconnected: for every open $U\subset S$, the closure
   $\overline U$ is open.
2. $S$ is projective for continuous surjections of compact Hausdorff spaces: for every
   continuous surjection $p\colon X\to Y$ of compact Hausdorff spaces and every continuous
   $f\colon S\to Y$ there is a continuous $g\colon S\to X$ with $p\circ g=f$.
3. Every continuous surjection $q\colon P\to S$ from a compact Hausdorff space $P$ has a
   continuous section.

Moreover an extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space is totally disconnected, hence
profinite.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib CompactT2.projective_iff_extremallyDisconnected, reversing the equivalence. Its proof is Gleason's minimal closed surjecting source argument, so the unit's projectivity characterization is retained.

source.place: CompactT2.projective_iff_extremallyDisconnected, lines 285–287; the forward and reverse implications are Projective.extremallyDisconnected and ExtremallyDisconnected.projective.

proof.text: A projective S has sections of compact Hausdorff surjections onto S: apply its lifting property to the identity S → S and the given surjection q.

Conversely, let p : X → Y be a continuous surjection of compact Hausdorff spaces and f : S → Y continuous. The product S × X is compact by the finite-product case of [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact] and Hausdorff by the product instance. Its equalizer P = {(s,x) | f(s) = p(x)} is closed by isClosed_eq, since Y is Hausdorff. Thus P is compact by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact] and Hausdorff as a subtype. The first projection q is continuous and surjective, by surjectivity of p. Apply the section hypothesis to q. The second projection of its continuous section σ is the lift: membership of σ(s) in P gives p(pr₂(σ(s))) = f(pr₁(σ(s))) = f(s).

source.place: Tag 08YN, pullback argument for projectivity from sections.
